buyer_question: Can we see every patient enquiry and follow-up status across phone, WhatsApp, booking and referral sources?
evidence_to_request: Redacted source list, status definitions, owner fields, callback SLA fields
hidden_risk_to_check: Leakage hidden outside core clinic workflow
when_aics_fits: AICS fits when owners need a source-to-owner evidence layer before replacement or integration
when_aics_does_not_fit: AICS does not fit when the buyer only needs routine software licensing or configuration
unsafe_claim_boundary: Do not claim AICS replaces clinical systems or guarantees appointments

buyer_question: Do reminders prove consent evidence, unresolved callbacks, human-review stops and owner ageing?
evidence_to_request: Redacted reminder categories, aggregate no-show/recall status, escalation rules
hidden_risk_to_check: Automated messaging without accountable owner review
when_aics_fits: AICS fits when follow-up gaps need operational evidence before campaign expansion
when_aics_does_not_fit: AICS does not fit when messaging scope and governance are already measured and owned
unsafe_claim_boundary: Do not claim no-show reduction, patient satisfaction or PDPA compliance

buyer_question: Which WhatsApp threads, missed calls and after-hours enquiries are stale or unsafe to automate?
evidence_to_request: Redacted queue export, response-stage labels, owner names/roles, escalation reasons
hidden_risk_to_check: Raw chats or phone logs shared unnecessarily
when_aics_fits: AICS fits when clinics need a no-credentials leak map and handoff rules
when_aics_does_not_fit: AICS does not fit when the need is only outsourced call answering capacity
unsafe_claim_boundary: Do not use patient identifiers, raw chats or medical claims in public proof

buyer_question: What conditions stop the AI and route to staff?
evidence_to_request: Human-review stop list, approved script scope, escalation owner matrix
hidden_risk_to_check: Clinical, emergency, medication, complaint or privacy request mishandled by automation
when_aics_fits: AICS fits before AI deployment to define evidence and safe boundaries
when_aics_does_not_fit: AICS does not fit when the buyer wants unsupervised medical/clinical automation
unsafe_claim_boundary: Do not claim AI accuracy, clinical safety or autonomous medical advice

buyer_question: Is operational evidence ready for adviser review?
hidden_risk_to_check: Compliance tooling detached from daily clinic workflows
when_aics_fits: AICS fits when operations need organized evidence and questions for advisers
when_aics_does_not_fit: AICS does not fit as legal counsel, DPO, auditor or regulator substitute
unsafe_claim_boundary: Do not claim certification, regulator approval or legal/privacy advice

best_for: No-credentials leakage and trust evidence map
buyer_question: Where are patient demand, owner handoff, consent questions and automation boundaries leaking before platform choice?
evidence_to_request: Redacted screenshots/exports, synthetic field mapping, aggregate counts, owner dashboard draft
hidden_risk_to_check: Mispositioning diagnostic work as proven client outcome
when_aics_fits: AICS fits for a fixed-scope evidence review before software, CRM or AI decisions
when_aics_does_not_fit: AICS does not fit if the buyer expects guaranteed revenue or production access-first implementation
unsafe_claim_boundary: Do not claim real clients, ROI, rankings, leads, revenue, compliance proof or outcomes
